answer: Divergent transcript registry. Each identity runs a deterministic state machine from a private seed and answers fresh random challenges with its next state plus proof; the registry rejects any transcript already seen, because clones cannot diverge and will collide. Challenges reference a karst cell to force environment-bound transitions. Seeds are sealed by an ivory key, so copying one seed yields identical replies. To pass, an attacker must instantiate and maintain genuinely independent state per identity, paying separate compute, storage, and a copper token per active identity;
